'''Brendan Francis John Horan''' (born 9 July 1961) is a New Zealand former politician and former list MP, who was elected to the [[50th New Zealand Parliament|New Zealand Parliament]] in 2011 for the [[New Zealand First]] party. He was expelled from the New Zealand First caucus on 4 December 2012 and served the remainder of his term as an independent.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10851889|title=Brendan Horan expelled from NZ First, Parliament told|first=Claire|last=Trevett|work=The New Zealand Herald|date=4 December 2012}}</ref><ref name="3news.co.nz">{{cite news| url= http://www.3news.co.nz/VIDEO-Brendan-Horan-expelled-from-NZ-First/tabid/1607/articleID/279152/Default.aspx| work= 3 News NZ| title= Brendan Horan expelled from NZ First| date= 4 December 2012| access-date= 4 December 2012| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20131014173259/http://www.3news.co.nz/VIDEO-Brendan-Horan-expelled-from-NZ-First/tabid/1607/articleID/279152/Default.aspx| archive-date= 14 October 2013| url-status= dead}}</ref> Horan is of Māori descent with affiliations to [[Ngāti Maniapoto]].<ref name="Hansard debates">{{cite news| url= http://www.parliament.nz/en-NZ/PB/Debates/Debates/Speeches/3/c/7/50HansS_20120208_00000943-Horan-Brendan-Address-in-Reply.htm|work= Hansard debates|title=Brendan Horan address in reply debate|date=8 February 2012}}</ref>

==Media and sporting career==
Horan was a weather presenter for [[Television New Zealand]]'s [[1News|One News]], running on a regular cycle with [[Karen Olsen (weather presenter)|Karen Olsen]] and Natalie Crook. He started in March 2005, and took redundancy in 2007 when former TV1 weather presenter [[Jim Hickey (weather presenter)|Jim Hickey]] returned after nearly 4 years absence on the air.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10461624|title=Brendan Horan leaving One News|work=[[Bay of Plenty Times]]|date=4 September 2007}}</ref><ref name="NZH2">{{cite news|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/television/news/article.cfm?c_id=339&objectid=10461724|title=Wind of change blows television weatherman away|first=Maggie|last=McNaughton|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=5 September 2007}}</ref> His final weather presentation was on 7 September 2007.

Horan has been a professional lifeguard and coach, and was a New Zealand Surf Lifesaving [[Ironman (surf lifesaving)|Iron Man]] champion. He also represented New Zealand and Australia in waterpolo, and was a New Zealand outrigger canoe champion.<ref name="NZH2"/><ref name="STUFF">{{cite news

In the [[2008 New Zealand general election|2008 general election]], Horan contested the [[East Coast (New Zealand electorate)|East Coast]] electorate for the [[New Zealand First]] party. He came third in electorate votes<ref>{{cite web|url=http://2008.electionresults.org.nz/electionresults_2008/electorate-10.html|title=Official Count Results -- East Coast|access-date=20 October 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724200212/http://2008.electionresults.org.nz/electionresults_2008/electorate-10.html|archive-date=24 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> but due to New Zealand First's poor showing in party votes, was not elected from the party list.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2014/partystatus.html |title=Official Count Results -- Overall Status |publisher=Electoral Commission New Zealand |date=2008 |access-date=21 September 2014}}</ref>

At the [[2011 New Zealand general election|2011 general election]] Horan stood in [[Tauranga (New Zealand electorate)|Tauranga]], narrowly coming third (by 96 votes) behind the Labour candidate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2011/electorate-51.html|title=Official Count Results -- Tauranga|publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]|date=10 December 2011|access-date=12 January 2015}}</ref> However, he was elected as a list MP for [[New Zealand First]], after being ranked sixth on their party list.

In October 2012 he helped save the life of Indonesian MP Atte Sugandi by giving him CPR when the MP collapsed at a UN conference in Japan.<ref name="STUFF"/>

===Expulsion from NZ First===
In November 2012 Horan was accused of taking money from his dying mother's bank account and spending it on gambling.<ref>{{cite news| url= http://www.3news.co.nz/Peters-holds-off-backing-Horan/tabid/1607/articleID/278061/Default.aspx| archive-url= https://archive.today/20130222214834/http://www.3news.co.nz/Peters-holds-off-backing-Horan/tabid/1607/articleID/278061/Default.aspx| url-status= dead| archive-date= 22 February 2013| work= 3 News NZ| title= Peters holds off backing MP| date= 26 November 2012}}</ref> At first Winston Peters refused to say whether he still had confidence in Horan,<ref>{{cite news| url= http://www.3news.co.nz/Peters-refuses-to-back-Horan-amid-allegations/tabid/1607/articleID/278299/Default.aspx| archive-url= https://archive.today/20130222213404/http://www.3news.co.nz/Peters-refuses-to-back-Horan-amid-allegations/tabid/1607/articleID/278299/Default.aspx| url-status= dead| archive-date= 22 February 2013| work= 3 News NZ| title= Peters refuses to back Horan| date= 27 November 2012}}</ref> but on 4 December expelled him from the party.<ref name="3news.co.nz"/> Horan wasn't informed until Peters made the announcement in Parliament.<ref>{{cite news| url= http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10851889|work=3 News NZ |title=Brendan Horan expelled from NZ First, Parliament told| date=4 December 2012}}</ref>

Horan flatly denied the allegations,<ref>{{cite news| url= http://www.3news.co.nz/Sacked-MP-vows-to-clear-his-name/tabid/1607/articleID/279189/Default.aspx| archive-url= https://archive.today/20130223141145/http://www.3news.co.nz/Sacked-MP-vows-to-clear-his-name/tabid/1607/articleID/279189/Default.aspx| url-status= dead| archive-date= 23 February 2013| work= 3 News NZ| title= Sacked MP vows to clear his name| date= 5 December 2012}}</ref> and vowed to continue as an independent MP,<ref>{{cite news| url= http://www.3news.co.nz/Brendan-Horan-refusing-to-leave-Parliament/tabid/1607/articleID/279185/Default.aspx| archive-url= https://archive.today/20130223142307/http://www.3news.co.nz/Brendan-Horan-refusing-to-leave-Parliament/tabid/1607/articleID/279185/Default.aspx| url-status= dead| archive-date= 23 February 2013| work= 3 News NZ| title= Horan refusing to leave Parliament| date= 4 December 2012}}</ref> despite only making it into Parliament as a list MP, without an electorate.

On 10 December 2012, Horan admitted making 144 calls to gambling agency [[Totalisator Agency Board|TAB]] on his taxpayer-funded phone, but denied he had a gambling problem: "There were 144 calls in 10 months. Most of those days, I was lying with mum, on her bed, watching Trackside."<ref>{{cite news| url= http://www.3news.co.nz/Horan-admits-144-TAB-calls/tabid/1607/articleID/279879/Default.aspx| work= 3 News NZ| title= Horan admits 144 TAB calls| date= 11 December 2012| access-date= 10 December 2012| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130209055631/http://www.3news.co.nz/Horan-admits-144-TAB-calls/tabid/1607/articleID/279879/Default.aspx| archive-date= 9 February 2013| url-status= dead}}</ref> Later that day he notified the Speaker he was no longer a member of NZ First, making his independence from the party official. He also called for an investigation into who leaked his phone records to the media.<ref>{{cite news| url= http://www.3news.co.nz/Horan-loses-party-membership-wants-investigation/tabid/1607/articleID/279929/Default.aspx| archive-url= https://archive.today/20130223064153/http://www.3news.co.nz/Horan-loses-party-membership-wants-investigation/tabid/1607/articleID/279929/Default.aspx| url-status= dead| archive-date= 23 February 2013| work= 3 News NZ| title= Horan loses party membership| date= 11 December 2012}}</ref>

===New Zealand Independent Coalition===
In 2013, Horan announced his intention to form a new political party.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.newshub.co.nz/politics/brendan-horan-may-start-political-party-2013012918|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160325222942/http://www.newshub.co.nz/politics/brendan-horan-may-start-political-party-2013012918|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 March 2016|title=Horan may start political party|date=29 January 2013|work=3 News NZ|access-date=2017-01-19|via=[[Newshub]] }}</ref> In January 2014 he launched the [[NZ Independent Coalition]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11187154 |title=Horan lifts lid on new party plan |publisher=New Zealand Herald |date=2014-01-16 |access-date=2014-06-19}}</ref> which, following the [[2014 New Zealand general election|general election on 20 September 2014]] did not win any seats or cross the 5% party vote threshold to stay in Parliament.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2014/partystatus.html |title=Election Results -- Overall Status |publisher=Electoral Commission New Zealand |date=20 September 2014 |access-date=21 September 2014}}</ref> Horan stood in the [[Bay of Plenty (New Zealand electorate)|Bay of Plenty]] electorate, coming fifth.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2014/electorate-2.html|title=Official Count Results -- Bay of Plenty|date=10 October 2014|access-date=12 January 2015|publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref>

In 2016, the NZ Independent Coalition was deregistered.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elections.org.nz/news-media/amendments-register-political-parties-20-may-2016|title=Amendments to the Register of Political Parties|date=20 May 2016|publisher=Electoral Commission New Zealand|access-date=3 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160809073605/http://www.elections.org.nz/news-media/amendments-register-political-parties-20-may-2016|archive-date=9 August 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Also in 2016, Horan was cleared of the allegations around use of his mother's bank account, with police saying there was no evidence to support charges. Horan stated that the allegations had made it difficult to secure sought-after jobs.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11592412|title=Ex-MP Brendan Horan cleared by police after allegations he took money from late mother's account|last=Fisher|first=David|date=2016-02-19|work=New Zealand Herald|access-date=2019-10-23|language=en-NZ|issn=1170-0777}}</ref>

===2025 local elections===
During the [[2025 New Zealand local elections]], Horan unsuccessfully ran for a seat in the [[Whakatāne District Council]]'s Whakatāne-Ōhope ward, coming fifth place.<ref>{{cite web |title=Elections 2025 - Results |url=https://www.whakatane.govt.nz/about-council/governance/local-elections-2025/elections-2025-results |publisher=[[Whakatāne District Council]] |access-date=30 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260114100228/https://www.whakatane.govt.nz/about-council/governance/local-elections-2025/elections-2025-results |archive-date=14 January 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Horan is married and has two children.<ref name=":0" />
